answer: Influence begins at a nadir of zero and does not rise until the key has lived through a lean season no disposable farm can subsidize. Climbing out requires a real-world anchor: a first unaffiliated payer who bonds slashable stake and attests that this key does not share a funder, host, or lock-step clock with any other. During that climb, payouts stay velvet — small, delayed, and fully clawed back if the key later fuses into a cluster — so minting a warehouse of quiet clones becomes a net loss rather than a shortcut.
